{
  "code": """"LightGBM baseline with consistent categorical encoding."""

from __future__ import annotations

import pandas as pd
from lightgbm import LGBMClassifier


def fit_predict(train_csv: str, test_rows: list[dict[str, str]]) -> list[float]:
    """Fit model on train data and predict probabilities for test rows.

    Returns one probability in [0, 1] per test row, preserving row order.
    Avoids interaction terms that may introduce noise given baseline near ceiling.
    """
    train = pd.read_csv(train_csv)
    y = train.pop("y").astype(int)
    
    # Build test DataFrame with same columns as train
    test = pd.DataFrame(test_rows)
    # Ensure column order matches train
    test = test[train.columns]
    
    # Process each column consistently
    for name in train.columns:
        if pd.api.types.is_numeric_dtype(train[name]):
            test[name] = pd.to_numeric(test[name], errors='coerce')
        else:
            # Get all categories from both train and test
            train_cats = set(train[name].unique())
            test_cats = set(test[name].unique())
            all_cats = sorted(train_cats | test_cats)
            
            train[name] = train[name].astype('category').cat.set_categories(all_cats)
            test[name] = test[name].astype('category').cat.set_categories(all_cats)
    
    # Simple LGBM without extra interaction terms
    model = LGBMClassifier(
        random_state=20261114,
        n_jobs=1,
        verbosity=-1,
        max_depth=6,
        learning_rate=0.05,
        n_estimators=200
    )
    model.fit(train, y)
    return model.predict_proba(test)[:, 1].tolist()
